BULLETIN 02 — THE PROBLEM

Payments need clearer recipient identity.

Wallet payments often require copying a long address. Recipient confirmation, exact approval and settlement evidence remain separate application responsibilities.

Public transfers can reveal counterparties and amounts. Network-specific asset and fee rules complicate payment routing and recovery.

TSN addresses the coordination layer: ten-digit payment identity, exact authorization, private-credit proof verification and reserve accounting.

Lost money
One wrong character and funds are gone. Address poisoning steals from wallets every year.
Lost privacy
Sender, recipient and balance metadata sit on-chain for anyone to read.
Lost time
Network, fee and transaction-state differences complicate recipient confirmation and recovery.
Missed mainstream
Recipient identity and clear approvals can improve the payment experience.

BULLETIN 03 — THE OFFER

A 10-digit identity
for money.

A human-facing recipient identifier that stays separate from settlement accounts. The owner signs the intent and separately approves wallet funding.

TIN
ten-digit identity with owner recovery
GPRU
hidden route and balance proof verification
TCAP
governed reserves and confidential accounting
“

TSN separates identity, intent verification, settlement authorization and asset accounting. Its hybrid model makes each participant's responsibility explicit while retaining the underlying blockchain's consensus and documented trust boundaries.

BULLETIN 04 — CURRENT EXPERIMENTAL FLOW

Wallet deposit to private TIN credit.
Owner authorization
Sign the TIN-targeted intent, then separately approve the exact TCAP reserve deposit.
Confirmed funding
Cranker submits the signed deposit unchanged; Node verifies the genuine asset-and-amount-bound funded leaf.
Private credit
Node prepares the hidden transition and Memo; Mother authorizes TSNP, and TCAP invokes GPRU before updating shared state.
Aggregate accounting
A separate proof covers 2–64 accepted credits and reclassifies their complete total. One confirmed deposit can support an individual credit.

Verified credentials
with owner consent.

A future extension could associate a provider-verified personal or business name with a TIN. Recipient confirmation would check the issuer, identity binding, validity and revocation while limiting disclosure.

BULLETIN 10 — PROPOSED OPERATING ECONOMICS

Costs and incentives follow the route.
Network cost
Wallet funding and settlement have chain fees. Sponsorship can cover a user's gas while retaining an actual operator cost.
Verification and operations
Proof preparation, durable coordination, monitoring and recovery need an evidenced operating and incentive model.
Future destination liquidity
Each EVM route must establish actual value delivery and any liquidity costs before offering a complete quote.
